title: Developer On-Ramp
text:
🚦 Developer On-Ramp Guide
Follow these six steps in order to get Pedalogical running locally.
Each step links to a detailed page in this documentation set.

Package Manager – install Homebrew (macOS) or Chocolatey (Windows)
→ Package Managers
Getting the Code – install Git and clone the repository
→ Git & Clone
Installing Tools – set up the .NET 9 SDK, EF Core CLI, VS Code, and extensions
→ .NET Tooling
Configuring Development Environment – create .env, add Postgres password & API keys
→ Environment Variables
Setting up Database – choose a native install or Docker + pgAdmin and start Postgres
→ Database Setup
Run the App – build, apply migrations, and launch the local API / UI
→ First Run

title: Package Managers
text:
We strongly recommend installing all tooling through a package manager — it keeps dependencies repeatable and easy to upgrade.


Homebrew installs under /opt/homebrew (Apple Silicon) or /usr/local (Intel).
/bin/bash -c "$(curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Homebrew/install/HEAD/install.sh)"
echo 'eval "$(/opt/homebrew/bin/brew shellenv)"' >> ~/.zprofile   # Apple Silicon
brew doctor          # Verify install


brew update          # refresh formulas
brew upgrade         # upgrade all packages




Chocolatey installs to C:\ProgramData\chocolatey.
Set-ExecutionPolicy Bypass -Scope Process -Force
[System.Net.ServicePointManager]::SecurityProtocol = 3072
iex ((New-Object System.Net.WebClient).DownloadString('https://community.chocolatey.org/install.ps1'))
choco upgrade chocolatey

Why not Winget?
Chocolatey covers everything we need and works on Server 2022 machines used in CI.








Next Step



Head to Git & Clone to install Git and pull the codebase.

title: Migration Guide for Existing Developers
text:
This page walks long‑time Pedalogical contributors through the key changes needed to align with our current tech stack.



We no longer store connection strings or API keys in appsettings.Development.json.
cp .env.example .env
code .env

Populate POSTGRES_PASSWORD, OPENAI_API_KEY, and any other keys shown in the template.

See full instructions → Environment Variables




Local development now uses PostgreSQL.
Follow either the native install or Docker‑Compose option.
See full instructions → Database Setup

After switching engines, apply EF Core migrations before running the app.





Run the app end‑to‑end to confirm the migration was successful.
Guide → Run the App
Checklist:

dotnet build succeeds.

EF Core migrations apply without errors.

API starts at https://localhost:5001/swagger.

Front‑end fetches sample data without 500s.

title: .NET Tooling
text:
Set up a .NET 9 development environment for Pedalogical. This guide covers installing the .NET SDK, EF Core CLI, and Visual Studio Code with recommended extensions.





Platform
Command




macOS
brew install --cask dotnet-sdk


Windows
choco install dotnet-9.0-sdk -y



Verify:
dotnet --version   # 9.x.x



dotnet tool install --global dotnet-ef
# add to PATH on macOS
echo 'export PATH="$HOME/.dotnet/tools:$PATH"' >> ~/.zprofile






macOS
Windows




brew install --cask visual-studio-code
choco install vscode -y



From VS Code Command Palette run:
Shell Command: Install 'code' command in PATH


code --install-extension ms-dotnettools.csdevkit
code --install-extension ms-dotnettools.csharp
code --install-extension jmrog.vscode-nuget-package-manager
code --install-extension ms-azuretools.vscode-docker
code --install-extension EditorConfig.EditorConfig







Next Step



Choose your preferred Database Setup path.

title: Database Migrations
text:
This guide covers how to manage database migrations, which are used to evolve the database schema as your C# models change.


From the root of the repository, run:
dotnet ef database update 



dotnet ef migrations add <Feature>
dotnet ef database update


<Verb><Entity><WhatChanged>
Examples:

AddStudentEmail
RenameCourseTable





dotnet ef migrations remove 



dotnet ef database update <MigrationName>



dropdb pedalogical           # native
createdb pedalogical
dotnet ef database update










Issue
Fix




Build failed
Ensure the solution builds before running dotnet ef.


No migrations were applied
You already ran them — verify with select * from __EFMigrationsHistory;.




🎉 You now have a fully functioning Pedalogical dev environment!

title: Database Setup
text:
Pedalogical uses PostgreSQL 17. Choose between a native install or Docker container.






Tip



Which method should I pick?
Docker is disposable, reproducible, and keeps your host clean.
Native is fine if you prefer brew services or need DB access when Docker isn’t running.






brew install postgresql@17
brew services start postgresql@17          # auto‑starts at login
brew install --cask pgadmin4          
Default data directory ➜ /opt/homebrew/var/postgresql@17



choco install postgresql17 -y
# Accept installer prompts and set the superuser password
pgAdmin is offered in the EnterpriseDB installer, or install via Chocolatey:
choco install pgadmin4 -y










macOS
Windows




brew install --cask docker
choco install docker-desktop -y



Launch Docker Desktop once to finish post‑install steps.






macOS
Windows




brew install --cask pgadmin4
choco install pgadmin4 -y






Make a copy of the example docker-compose.yml file:
cd ~/GitHub/AiTutor/Docker
cp docker-compose.example.yml docker-compose.yml
Edit docker-compose.yml and set the Postgres superuser password (obtain from Team Notion):
environment:
  POSTGRES_PASSWORD: "Password"



docker-compose up -d
docker ps           # verify 'pedalogical-db' is healthy
Ports (default):



Service
Host Port




Postgres
5433


pgAdmin
8080








Open http://localhost:8080
Add new server:
Host : host.docker.internal (mac/Win)
Port: 5433








Next Step



Run the App.

title: Git & Clone
text:
Install Git and clone the Pedalogical repository to your local machine.





Platform
Install
Verify




macOS
brew install git
git --version


Windows
choco install git -y
git --version




If macOS prompts for Xcode Command‑Line Tools, accept the install — Homebrew relies on them.




ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -C "you@willamette.edu"
pbcopy < ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub   # macOS
cat ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub        # Windows Git Bash
Add the key to your GitHub account (Settings → SSH Keys).



We keep all project repos in ~/GitHub for consistency.
cd ~
mkdir -p GitHub && cd GitHub
git clone git@github.com:wu-software-lab/AiTutor.git   # SSH
# or
git clone https://github.com/wu-software-lab/AiTutor.git  # HTTPS
cd AiTutor
git status


git remote add upstream https://github.com/wu-software-lab/AiTutor.git
git pull upstream main







Next Step



Configure your Environment Variables.

title: Welcome
text:
Pedalogical Developer On‑Ramp 🚀
Welcome to the Pedalogical Developer Docs — your single source of truth for getting a local development environment up and running in less than 30 minutes (coffee not included ☕).
Whether you are:

Totally new to the project and need everything installed,

Migrating from our former SQL Server stack, or

Returning after a hiatus and just need a refresher,


Pro Tip
Keep a terminal open next to these docs and copy‑paste as you go. Most commands are idempotent — if you run them twice nothing breaks.

title: First App Run
text:
Run the app to create the database and seed initial data.


From the root of the repository, run:
dotnet ef database update



You can check the database using your preferred PostgreSQL client (e.g., pgAdmin, BeeHive, or command line). Look for the pedalogical database and verify that the initial tables and data are present.
To verify via command line, you can run:
psql -U postgres -d pedalogical -c "\dt"
You should see tables like AspNetUsers, AspNetRoles, and others that were seeded during the initial run.



Run the application to create the initial data:
dotnet run



Open your browser and navigate to http://localhost:5000 to access the application.




Click on the “Register” link.
Fill out the registration form and submit it.
Check your email for a confirmation link (it might be in your spam folder).
Log in with the new account.











Issue
Fix




Database connection error
Ensure your .env file has the correct POSTGRES_PASSWORD and that the database is running.


Application not starting
Check the console output for errors, ensure all dependencies are installed, and that the database is initialized.


Email not sending
Verify you are connected to the internet and check your spam folder.
